summary: Package reuse enforcement, COUX/FED-COUX cost control, row signal injection, multi-sink handoff and measurement requirements for Pen processing.

programs.name: reuse_enforcement
actions: Add reuse check at WIP, Pen and Symbio ingress.
Use registry match before creating new build work.
Record reuse decision and route evidence.
Create new work only when reuse score is low and gap is logged.

programs.name: coux_fed_coux_cost_control
actions: COUX owns fast-path routing and packaging.
FED-COUX runs only for multi-specialist or cross-thread synthesis.
GDrive worker remains stub only until service account is configured.
Retries run only for failed or receipt-missing jobs.

programs.name: thread_signal_injection
actions: Use x_t4h metadata fields on rows and records.
Fields: signal, agent, scope, priority, action, receipt_required, idempotency_key, evidence_state.
Exclude secrets, full prompts, large blobs and mutable canonical business truth.
Map signals to queued work, not direct execution.

programs.name: multi_sink_handoff
actions: Pen receives executable JSON pointer job.
Supabase receives runtime and audit records.
Large artefacts use pointer plus checksum.
Human-readable docs are optional supporting artefacts.
Close only when receipt or evidence exists.

workers.name: coux-router
workers.responsibility: Fast-path route, reuse lookup, package, enqueue

workers.name: retry-daemon
workers.responsibility: Retry failed or missing-receipt jobs with idempotency

workers.name: queue-monitor
workers.responsibility: Detect queue drops and stalled runs

workers.name: audit-sweeper
workers.responsibility: Find missing evidence and invalid closure

workers.name: gdrive-worker
workers.responsibility: Disabled until service account is configured

acceptance_criteria: Pen creates or references a processing receipt.
Every job has idempotency_key, route, expected output and validator.
No complete state without receipt or evidence.
GDrive worker stays stubbed until configured.
FED-COUX skipped for single structured output.
Metrics exist for throughput, latency, retries, drift and cost per job.
